Key Research Thinking Patterns: Connect Frameworks to Health: Links abstract social constructs and cultural norms to concrete health behaviors (e.g. connects feminine honor ideology to HPV vaccination intentions, links chronic disease status to long-term smoking habits).

Methodological Innovation: Innovates and refines statistical methods to solve complex data problems (e.g. co-developing random rPQL algorithm for variable selection, establishing workflow for clustering intensive longitudinal data).
Rigorous Validation: Validates research through large-scale simulations and long-term cohort studies (e.g. using extensive simulation studies to test new statistical algorithms).
Challenging Assumptions: Challenges existing assumptions and investigates understudied research problems (e.g. questioning “gender independence” of honor culture).
Summary Description: Hairong Song is a researcher in psychological methods and health psychology, focusing on how cultural frameworks and individual health status shape behaviors like HPV vaccination and long-term smoking. Her work bridges methodological innovation with pressing social and health challenges, using rigorous methods like simulation studies and longitudinal analysis to improve how researchers analyze complex data. Song explores unexamined assumptions in cultural psychology and methodological gaps in statistical modeling to provide innovative tools and data-driven insights into complex human dynamics and health behaviors.
